chunks: He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servants, and He is more Knowing of what is in the chests, more Seeing of what is in the eyes, Closer to what is in the bellies, and More Capable of what He wills. Nothing can overpower Him, He does not neglect anything, He does not forget anything, He does not err from anything, Nothing hidden escapes Him, Nothing absent is lost to Him, Nothing missed escapes Him, No secret is concealed from Him, No open matter is hidden from Him, No apparent thing is absent from Him, No inner reality is hidden from Him.

key_terms.ظَلَّامٍ: Tyrant or one who does injustice

ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and knowledge mentioned in this narration?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to anchor the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*) within the broader framework of God's omniscience, arguing that His perfect knowledge precludes any possibility of negligence (*Ghaflah*) or forgetfulness (*Nisyan*). This serves as a theological rebuttal to those who attribute human-like limitations to the Divine, affirming that His power and awareness are absolute and encompass both the manifest and the hidden realms.
